note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 18(7), DOR 1, 5, 7; A06b Const 18(7), DOR 1, 5, 7; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 2 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: Parental residence restriction) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Dominican Republic, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in the DR for at least 2 years uninterrupted. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in the DR to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen. If person also obtains another citizenship at birth, citizenship can either be retained or renounced by declaration when he/she reaches the age of majority. ... Parental residence restriction ... Person is born in the DR. Unless born to foreign diplomats, foreigners 'in transit', and those residing illegally in the country. ... No provision
